The result depends on Cloudflare\'s nearest site and its route (the site\'s code, e.g. SIN for Singapore, is stored with the result), and many large tests in a row are blocked for a while (HTTP 429).
Start and stop it on the Live screen while a session is logging. One capture per session; it stops when the session stops.
NetLogger runs its own VPN on the phone. Android asks you once to allow it. Only one VPN can run at a time, so turn off any other VPN first.

It records the IP traffic between each app and the VPN, and which app owns each connection. It does not see radio signalling, and packet sizes and timing are rebuilt by the VPN, not the ones on the air.
The session export adds capture.pcap (open it in Wireshark), capture_sync.csv (clock alignment with the radio log) and connections.csv (the app of each connection).
Files grow with the traffic: a speed test during a capture adds about 100 MB to the pcap. Speed tests during a capture are flagged, because the capture slows them down.
Applies to the next capture. Traffic of apps not chosen bypasses the VPN and is not recorded.
Everything the phone sends and receives, including background apps and system services.
Only the apps you tick below, e.g. one video app for a QoE test. Smaller files that are easier to analyse.
No app selected yet: until you tick one, all apps are captured.
Only apps with an icon in the app drawer are listed. Include NetLogger itself to capture its speed tests.
The largest packet the VPN passes on. Applies to the next capture; the value is stored with it.
The same packet sizes as on a mobile network, so the pcap looks like real traffic. Fast links lose up to a quarter of their download speed during the capture.
Hardly slows the phone down (about 3 percent), but packets are bigger than on the air. Use it when throughput matters more than packet sizes.

NetLogger records what the phone\'s modem reports about the mobile network, together with GPS, battery and data use, once per interval. These pages explain how to get clean, comparable data.

string-array.name: help_start
string-array.item: Allow precise location, phone and notifications when NetLogger asks. Without them it cannot log, but recorded sessions can still be viewed and exported.
Turn Wi-Fi off for mobile measurements. With Wi-Fi on, mobile data idles, the phone often stays off 5G, and speed tests are refused.
Set NetLogger\'s battery use to Unrestricted in Android\'s app settings, so logging keeps its pace with the screen off. Settings › Phone capabilities shows the current state.
Fix the phone in a holder with a view of the sky for GPS, and use the same position for every run you want to compare. The screen may be off while logging.
For long tests, start with a full battery or use a charger. Charging changes the battery values that are logged.

string-array.name: help_test
string-array.item: On Live, choose the scenario in the menu at the top (Drive, Walk, Static or Indoor), then tap Start. The bar at the top shows the recording time and the number of intervals recorded. A notification stays while NetLogger records, also with the screen off.

Live shows the operator and network type, the serving cells (LTE and 5G side by side; SS marks a value the phone reported only in its signal-strength report, not with the cell), GPS, and where the data goes (mobile network, or Wi-Fi with its name) with the download and upload rate averaged over 5 seconds, and the last events (cell changes with the signal before and after, 5G added or removed, GPS lost). Details at the bottom holds every raw value, the battery and the parse warnings.
Marker, on Live or Add marker in the notification, stores the time and place of something worth noting, e.g. a tunnel, a call drop or the start of a route section.
Gray values on Live are older than 5 seconds: the phone did not report anything newer. They are stored as reported, with their age, so they can be filtered later.
Stop ends the session. If Android closes the app during a session, the session is closed at the next start and keeps every row recorded until then.
Sessions lists your recordings: open one to rename it, add notes, see charts, export or delete it.

string-array.name: help_speed
string-array.item: While a session is logging, with Wi-Fi off, start it on Live: Private server tests against your own server, set in Settings › Speed test (a LibreSpeed server works); Cloudflare tests against Cloudflare\'s public servers and needs no setting. Stop ends a test early and keeps the parts already finished.
It measures ping, then download and upload for 10 seconds each. One test can use up to about 250 MB of your data plan.

The result depends on the radio (signal, 4G or 5G, how busy the cell is) and on the route to the server. Compare tests against the same server; Cloudflare is only for comparison. With Cloudflare, the site that answered is stored with the result (e.g. SIN for Singapore): a far site means a longer route.

string-array.name: help_capture
string-array.item: Start it in the Capture row on Live while a session is logging. Android asks once to allow NetLogger\'s VPN. The capture stops with Stop or at the end of the session.
Only one VPN can run at a time: turn other VPN apps off first. connections.csv lists which app owns each connection.
Choose all apps or specific apps, and the packet size (MTU), in Settings › Traffic capture.
Files grow with the traffic: a speed test during a capture adds about 100 MB.
It records the apps\' IP traffic, not radio signalling, and packet sizes and timing are rebuilt by the VPN. Speed tests during a capture are flagged because the capture slows them down.

string-array.name: help_results
string-array.item: Map colours a session\'s track by LTE RSRP, NR SS-RSRP, LTE or NR SINR, or network type. Tap a point to see its values.
Open a session in Sessions for charts of the signal over time and the network type.

Save ZIP or Share ZIP exports one session: session.json (phone, SIM, settings), measurements.csv (one row per interval), cells.csv (serving and neighbour cells), events.csv, throughput.csv, warnings.csv, flat.csv (one row per interval with the main values; easiest for Excel) and track.geojson. With a capture also capture.pcap, capture_sync.csv and connections.csv.
CSV files use commas and a dot for decimals. If Excel shows everything in one column, open the file with Data › From Text/CSV and choose comma as the delimiter.
Open capture.pcap in Wireshark. Packet times use the same clock as the radio log; capture_sync.csv shows how they line up.

string-array.name: help_problems
string-array.item: If NetLogger crashes, freezes, or Android ends it during a recording, a red card on Live says so the next time you open it. The recording is closed and keeps everything recorded until then.

Settings › Problem reports keeps these reports on the phone (at most 20). Open one to see exactly what would be sent: the app and phone model, what happened, a technical trace and NetLogger\'s own log lines; no location, cell identities, Wi-Fi names or captured traffic.
Send a report with Share (e-mail, chat) or as a GitHub issue, which is public. Nothing is sent automatically. When you come back, NetLogger asks whether it was sent, so you can delete it.
For a native crash you may also attach the raw crash dump. It helps the developer, but it can contain parts of NetLogger\'s memory, so only attach it when you trust the receiver.
Something wrong without a crash? Use Describe a problem and say what you did, what happened and what you expected.

string-array.name: help_glossary
string-array.item: RSRP: received power of a cell\'s reference signal, in dBm. About −80 is strong, below −110 weak.
RSRQ: signal quality in dB, lower with interference and load. About −10 is good, below −15 poor.
SINR: signal to interference and noise, in dB. Above 20 is excellent, below 0 poor. LTE phones report it as RSSNR, scaled differently by each maker.
PCI: physical cell ID (0 to 503 in LTE, 0 to 1007 in 5G NR). Not unique; together with the channel it tells cells apart.

Cell ID (LTE ECI): the 28-bit identity of an LTE cell, shown on Live as Cell and exported as ciOrNci (cells.csv) and lteCi (flat.csv). It holds the eNB (the base station) and the cell on it: eNB ID = ECI ÷ 256 without the remainder, local cell ID = the remainder. In Excel: =INT(lteCi/256) and =MOD(lteCi,256); e.g. 12866888 is eNB 50261, cell 72. A 5G NR cell ID (NCI) cannot be split this way: each operator chooses how many of its bits are the gNB.
EARFCN / NR-ARFCN: channel number of an LTE or 5G carrier; gives its frequency.
Band: frequency range of the carrier, e.g. LTE B3 (1800 MHz) or 5G n40 (2300 MHz).
NSA and SA: 5G non-standalone uses an LTE cell as anchor and adds 5G for data; standalone uses 5G alone.
CA: carrier aggregation, several carriers used at once for more speed.
TA: timing advance, a rough distance from the cell.
CQI: channel quality indicator that the phone sends to the network (0 to 15).

Cell change: the serving cell\'s PCI or channel changed. It may be a handover (during a connection) or a reselection (while idle); Android\'s public interfaces do not tell which, so NetLogger does not label it.

resources.string: No problems recorded · describe a problem

When NetLogger crashes, freezes, or Android ends it during a recording, a report is kept here. Reports stay on this phone until you send one; nothing is sent automatically. A report contains the app and phone model, what happened and NetLogger\'s own log lines, but no location, cell identities, Wi-Fi names or captured traffic.
This is exactly what will be sent. Check it first.
Also attach the raw crash dump

Helps the developer with native crashes. It is Android\'s full dump of the crash: besides the trace above it can contain parts of NetLogger\'s memory and its recent log, unfiltered, which may include location or network data.

Issues on github.com/mppamungkas/netlogger are public: anyone can read the report. You need a GitHub account. The browser opens a new issue with the report filled in; the full report is also copied to the clipboard, in case it had to be shortened.
NetLogger cannot see whether you sent it in the other app. If it reached GitHub or the person you shared it with, it can be deleted from this phone.

Something wrong without a crash, e.g. values that look wrong or a screen that does not react? Describe what you did, what happened and what you expected. NetLogger\'s last log lines are added; you see the whole report before sending it.

string-array.name: about_privacy
string-array.item: Sessions and exports contain your precise location and track, the cells you used (which also give your location) and your phone model and SIM operator. Share them only with people who need them.
A traffic capture contains the network traffic of the captured apps: which servers they contact, and the content of anything not encrypted. Handle capture files like private data.
Problem reports (crashes, freezes) stay on the phone until you send one yourself; they contain no location, cell identities, Wi-Fi names or captured traffic.

Everything stays on the phone until you export it. NetLogger has no account, no analytics and no upload. It contacts only the map tile server (OpenStreetMap, for the area you view), your speed test server when you run a test (or Cloudflare when you run a Cloudflare test), and Google Play services, which provides the location.
